adr_madr_0001-use-CC0-or-MIT-as-license.notes: Strong options analysis with 6 genuine alternatives and pros/cons per option. SPDX identifier makes it highly actionable. Gaps: decision drivers not in explicit list format; no status field in frontmatter. DQ strong across Q2/Q7.

adr_madr_0002-do-not-use-numbers-in-head.notes: Has 2 options and a justified outcome. All 3 rationale bullets are positives only — no negatives documented (Q6=0). No drivers, no status, no trade-off analysis. Context too brief for the decision scope.

adr_madr_0003-provide-own-madr-tools.notes: Highest SC of the batch. 5 options with star-count evidence. Explicit negative consequence (maintenance cost). Non-standard status on hold fails C7. Q6 rated 1 — only one consequence stated with no explicit positives.

adr_madr_0004-write-own-toc-tool.notes: Good consequence objectivity (explicit good/bad) and strong actionability (exact npm command). Rationale weakened by acknowledging extending adr-tools is also possible. Only 2 options. No drivers. No status.

adr_madr_0005-use-dashes-in-filenames.notes: Strongest DQ criteria coverage of the batch (Q3=2 across all dimensions). Format specified exactly (NNNN-title.md, @ADR(1) syntax). No consequences section at all — Q6=0. No drivers, no status. Good rationale but no trade-off analysis.

adr_madr_0006-use-names-as-identifier.notes: Explicit drivers present. No consequences, no status. 2 options only. Good rationale on no markdown ID standard and readability. Q4=0, Q6=0 recurring MADR pattern.

adr_madr_0007-do-not-emphasize-line-head.notes: Minor formatting decision with limited architectural significance (Q1=1). Two solid rationale bullets. No consequences, no trade-off analysis. No status field.

adr_madr_0008-add-status-field.notes: Best Q6 in batch: extensive good/bad for all 6 options with examples. 6 realistic options well-researched. No explicit drivers section. No status (ironic). Outcome line thin but pros/cons are comprehensive.

adr_madr_0009-support-links-between-adrs.notes: 6 options including Do Not Add Links. CommonMark compliance used as consistent criterion. Outcome rationale weak but pros/cons carry it. No drivers, no status.

adr_madr_0010-support-categories.notes: Strongest ADR in batch — 1pt below Fully Compliant. 6 drivers, 7 options with concrete folder examples. Good/bad for all options. No status field only gap.

adr_madr_0011-use-asterisk-as-list-marke.notes: Low-scope decision. Neutrality argument specific and well-cited (Markdown Style Guide). No consequences, no drivers, no status. Mirrors 0007 profile.

adr_madr_0012-use-curly-braces-to-denote.notes: Q7=3: specific syntax with real user failure modes documented. Exception for bare templates shows nuanced thinking. Q6=2: real user behavior as evidence for rejecting square brackets. No drivers, no status.

adr_madr_0013-use-yaml-front-matter-for-.notes: Q6=3: 3 explicit Bads for chosen option including rendering not standardized and parser compatibility. Remarkably honest consequence section. ADR about status fields has no status field (C7 fail).

adr_madr_0014-allow-neutral-arguments.notes: High word count but bulk is illustrative examples not analysis. Q5=1: fits best and +/0/- pattern are thin justifications. Q6=1: only OK option gets real-world example; others have no analysis.

adr_madr_0015-include-consulting-informe.notes: High SC. Q6=1: Do Not Include option has no pros/cons despite being viable. Q5=2: Accountable/Responsible confusion and consensus-team scenario are specific and convincing. No status.

adr_madr_0016-outcome-before-detailed-pr.notes: Q5=3: best rationale in batch — appendix analogy, above-the-fold principle, logical flow all clearly chained. Q4=2: priority explicitly stated. Q2=1: only 2 options is real gap. Duplicate bullet in not-chosen option (copy-paste).

adr_madr_0017-use-same-format-for-outcom.notes: Weakest DQ in batch. Outcome is one line: resolves all forces — completely unsupported. No pros/cons, no consequences despite 3 options and explicit drivers. Real problem identified but not justified.

adr_madr_0018-use-confirmation-as-headin.notes: Q5=3: sharpest semantic reasoning in full batch — validation/verification/confirmation distinction expertly argued. Q7=3: timed actionable steps. Q6=0: Confirmation section is implementation steps not decision consequences — rubric distinction matters. 1pt below Mostly Compliant.

alphagov_content-publisher_0001-record-a.notes: Identical to govuk-aws meta-ADR. 59 words. No options, no drivers, consequences deferred to Nygard article. Lowest possible score for a structurally-present ADR.

alphagov_content-publisher_0002-use-loca.notes: SC=100: all 7 criteria pass. 4 explicit We-want-to bullets serve as drivers. Q5=3: Specialist Publisher experience cited as concrete evidence. Q6=3: acknowledges sync pain and need to update GOV.UK Architecture Goals. Exemplary Nygard ADR.

alphagov_content-publisher_0003-initial-.notes: Three sub-decisions with explicit trade-offs each. Exceptional intellectual honesty: we are insufficiently informed. Q6=3: three specific risk paragraphs including user experience risk from Whitehall-inconsistent localization model.

alphagov_content-publisher_0004-editing-.notes: High word count (1088). C3 fails: no explicit driver list. Q7=3: 7 specific extraction rules with code paths. Q4=1: option 3 chosen by trial not formal criteria weighting. Positive: non-developer empowerment consequence specific and measurable.

alphagov_content-publisher_0005-avoiding.notes: Interim decision explicitly labeled — intellectual honesty point. Q7=3: code snippets for Options 2 and 3. Q3=1: only UX dimension covered; accessibility and broader browser support not assessed. Specific users affected (JS-enabled but JS-failed) in consequences.

alphagov_content-publisher_0006-tagging-.notes: Consequences section is entirely reference links — zero prose. Q6=0: most significant gap. Decision rationale (4 specific Whitehall flaws) is well-argued but no consequences documented. Superseded status correctly captured (C7 PASS).

alphagov_content-publisher_0007-minimal-.notes: No Considered Options at all (C4=F). Q2=0. Q7=3: specific class names (DocumentType, Supertype) and directory paths given. Prescriptive definition without defending it against alternative classification approaches.

alphagov_content-publisher_0008-restrict.notes: Clean simplest-thing decision with honest negative consequence (GDPR deletion difficulty). C3 fails. Option comparison embedded in context prose. Q6=2: development environment workaround noted alongside GDPR risk.

alphagov_content-publisher_0009-modellin.notes: Most architecturally significant ADR in the full dataset (2881 words). Six sub-decisions: Document/Edition/Revision/Status concepts, immutability strategy, pessimistic vs optimistic locking, image modelling, timeline, topics. Q5=3: concurrent editing locking scenario with before/after walkthroughs exceptional. C4=F: immutability assumed not defended vs event sourcing or audit tables.

alphagov_content-publisher_0010-sending-.notes: Classic inverted ADR: DQ=82 but SC=70. No alternatives to Notify+ActionMailer+ActiveJob+Sidekiq explored (C4=F). Within that solution every sub-choice rigorously justified. Q6=3: 4 specific consequences including Sidekiq visibility loss, Markdown limitation, individual API call volume.

alphagov_content-publisher_0011-moving-b.notes: 5 genuine alternatives evaluated (Service objects, dry-transaction, Interactor, Trailblazer, pub-api command). Q2=3. Q7=3: directory structure, naming convention, scope rules all specified. Bikeshedding as explicit anti-pattern notable. C3 missing only gap.

alphagov_content-publisher_0012-file-att.notes: Q6=3 standout: 3 numbered consequences including non-obvious cyclic dependency (Govspeak/GOV.UK Publishing Components) and its resolution (Kramdown). Future-facing Content API consequence shows long-horizon thinking. C3 fails.

alphagov_content-publisher_0013-permitte.notes: Correctly references and supersedes ADR-08 — cross-referencing done well. Security context change well-argued. Q7=3: specific FK constraint changes linked to actual commits. C3 fails but context is strong.

alphagov_content-publisher_0014-politica.notes: Lowest DQ in batch. Reads as implementation spec not architecture decision. No alternatives (C4=F). Q2=0, Q4=0. system_political vs editor_political distinction interesting but not defended vs alternatives. Explicit timeout risk consequence is positive.

alphagov_content-publisher_0015-bulk-dat.notes: Q6=3 and Q7=3 bright spots: 15-min interval, 24-hr TTL, 503 on empty cache, queue flood prevention, implementation links. No alternatives to Redis/Whitehall pattern (C4=F). DQ pulled down by Q2=0, Q4=0.

alphagov_content-publisher_0016-publishi.notes: Only perfect-scoring ADR in the full dataset (all three batches). 4 explicitly named problems, 3 realistic alternatives, bold architectural judgment (Publishing API ChangeNote model fundamentally flawed) backed by 3 specific observations, 6 consequence paragraphs including field-level schema and deprecation reversal. Exemplar for paper.

npryce_adr-tools_0004-markdown-format.notes: Strong short ADR for Markdown decision records. It states plain-text constraints, version-control needs, formatting needs, and practical output consequences. Alternatives are implicit rather than formal.

npryce_adr-tools_0005-help-comments.notes: Good help-comments ADR. It explains why usage docs should live near script code and records both maintainability benefits and lack of automated consistency checks. Alternatives are not explicit.

npryce_adr-tools_0006-packaging-and-dist.notes: Clear packaging and distribution ADR. It explains why downstream repositories should handle packaging and records useful consequences, but alternatives are implied rather than explicitly compared.

npryce_adr-tools_0007-invoke-adr-config-.notes: Concise configuration ADR with a clear packager problem and executable adr-config decision. It lacks an explicit alternatives section, but consequences and actionability are adequate.

npryce_adr-tools_0008-use-iso-8601-forma.notes: Strong small ADR. It compares UK date formatting with ISO 8601, explains ambiguity and culture-neutral formatting, and documents practical compatibility consequences.

npryce_adr-tools_0009-help-scripts.notes: Short amendment ADR for generated help scripts. It is clear and actionable, but alternatives and prioritization are thin and the consequence analysis is limited.

openfga_openfga_architecture.notes: This is high-level architecture documentation, not an ADR. It describes OpenFGA components and deployment shape but does not record a decision, options, rationale, consequences, or status.

temporalio_temporal_chasm.notes: This is architecture documentation for CHASM concepts and entities. It explains the framework but does not document a specific decision, alternatives, status, or consequences.

temporalio_temporal_effect-package.notes: Small design note for the effect package. It gives motivation and usage for callback buffering after persistence, but lacks ADR structure, alternatives, explicit status, and consequence analysis.

temporalio_temporal_history-service.notes: This is internal architecture documentation for the History Service. It is detailed and useful, but it does not record a single decision with options, rationale, status, and consequences.

temporalio_temporal_matching-service.notes: This is a brief Matching Service architecture overview. It describes task queues and partitions but does not function as an ADR.

temporalio_temporal_nexus.notes: This is internal documentation for Nexus RPC implementation in Temporal. It contains architecture detail but lacks ADR status, considered options, decision outcome, and consequences.

temporalio_temporal_retry.notes: This is package-level documentation for retry primitives and service errors. It is not an architecture decision record and has no explicit decision or alternatives.

temporalio_temporal_workflow-update.notes: Detailed internal implementation design for Workflow Update with strong requirements, lifecycle, API, state machine, timeout, race, and persistence discussion. It is not structured as an ADR and lacks explicit alternatives and status.

thomvaill_log4brains_20200924-use-markdo.notes: Strong ADR for adopting MADR with a Log4brains patch. It lists several viable record formats, gives clear rationale, and records status and date. Consequences are mostly embedded in the decision outcome rather than separated.

thomvaill_log4brains_20200925-multi-pack.notes: Strong initial architecture ADR. It compares monolith, multirepo, and monorepo options, ties the choice to extensibility and package publication, and gives useful project-specific rationale.

thomvaill_log4brains_20200925-use-pretti.notes: Complete code-style ADR with many considered linting and formatting options. The rationale is practical but relatively brief, relying mainly on popularity and reduced debate.

thomvaill_log4brains_20200926-use-the-ad.notes: Clear superseded identifier ADR. It compares ADR number, filename, and title and gives concise rationale around uniqueness, command-line usability, and existing ADR-tool precedent.

thomvaill_log4brains_20201016-use-the-ad.notes: Good superseding ADR that fixes merge conflicts caused by numeric ADR identifiers. It is actionable and explains sorting rules, but it does not explicitly revisit alternatives.

thomvaill_log4brains_20201026-the-core-a.notes: Complete ADR for placing MDX enhancement in the core API. It identifies future VSCode extension needs, compares UI versus core responsibility, and records positive and negative consequences.

thomvaill_log4brains_20201103-use-lunr-f.notes: Strong search ADR. It lists clear drivers, compares Fuse.js and Lunr.js, and justifies Lunr based on serialized indexes, fast searching, stemming, language support, and match positions.

thomvaill_log4brains_20210113-distribute.notes: Good distribution ADR. It explains why the previous JS-project-oriented setup failed for non-JS projects and gives a language-agnostic global npm package decision with implementation consequences.

thomvaill_log4brains_20240926-transition.notes: Excellent process ADR. It states release and delegation problems, lists decision drivers, compares GitHub Flow, Simplified Git Flow, and full Git Flow, and records positive and negative consequences.

thomvaill_log4brains_20241217-switch-bac.notes: Strong superseding workflow ADR. It explains Lerna limitations, preserves beta-release goals, compares patching Lerna with returning to GitHub Flow, and gives a clear selected outcome.

alphagov_govuk-aws_0038-mongo_replacemen.notes: No alternatives to DocumentDB considered, such as MongoDB Atlas or self-managed MongoDB v4. Q6=3 because the ADR lists five specific negative consequences: null character limitation, authentication changes, super-user caveat, FQDN lock-in, and backup tooling changes with govuk_env_sync. Q7=3 because exact MongoDB versions are cited, including 3.2.7 and 2.4.9. C3 and C4 fail.

alphagov_govuk-aws_0026-remove-load-bala.notes: Incomplete ADR. Two ADR TODO: TBC references defer risks and the domain split to an unwritten future ADR. The record is very short at 211 words. It has no options and no criteria. Q5, Q6, and Q7 are low because important rationale and consequences are deferred. This is a real-world example of a structurally present but substantively incomplete ADR.

loopdive_js2_0001-hybrid-compilation-str.notes: One point below Fully Compliant; the only structural gap is C3 because decision drivers are embedded in prose. Strong Q5=3: the proven-invariants-only principle is grounded in program analysis theory, and the boundary thunk approach targets the exact failure mode. Four alternatives are explicitly rejected with specific reasons. The ADR cross-references ADR-009, ADR-002, and ADR-010.

loopdive_js2_0004-aot.notes: Very strong DQ score. Three alternatives are compared with exact performance and size details, including 25-50x slower interpreter behavior and 2MB+ JIT overhead. Q5=3 because serverless and edge hosts disabling runtime code generation is specific and verifiable. Q6=3 because eval() and dynamic import() are named as explicit feature-level limitations. The static versus dynamic eval() distinction is actionable.

MITLibraries_timdex-ui_0001-record-archi.notes: Fourth instance of the classic meta-ADR pattern in the dataset. It has the same profile as govuk-aws-0001 and content-publisher-0001. Consequences are deferred to the Nygard article. This is useful as a systematic real-world pattern of structurally present but substantively weak ADRs.

MITLibraries_timdex-ui_0002-extend-timde.notes: Five options are well analyzed with specific limitations, including flipflop maintenance concerns, direct-link breakage for search params, and the header-only limitation of the theme gem. Q6=1 because consequences are comparatively vague; overabstraction risk and unforeseeable use cases are not concrete negatives. C3 fails because drivers are embedded in prose.
